outlook.discussion: 1. Offshore of the East Coast of the United States (AL93): A storm-force non-tropical low pressure area located a few hundred miles off the mid-Atlantic United States coast has acquired some subtropical characteristics since yesterday, including some organized thunderstorm activity and less defined frontal features near the center. This system has the potential to become a subtropical storm tonight or early Thursday as it accelerates to the northeast before upper-level winds and water temperatures become unfavorable for further development on Friday. 1. 2. Subtropical Central Atlantic: A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles east-southeast of Bermuda is producing a large area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Some development of this system is possible during the next day or two while it moves slowly north-northeastward. Upper-level winds are forecast to become too strong for further development by the weekend. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

1. Western Central Pacific: An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International Date Line, a few hundred miles southwest of Johnston Atoll late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.
